stem:
A 58-year-old woman with progressive pruritus and dark urine has scleral icterus and elevated direct bilirubin. Right-upper-quadrant ultrasound shows dilated intrahepatic bile ducts but a normal gallbladder.

Which of the following best explains why her hepatocytes continue to produce bile despite impaired delivery to the duodenum?

options.label: A
options.text: Bile synthesis is a continuous hepatic function independent of downstream duct patency
options.misconception: None; hepatocytes keep making bile even when outflow is obstructed, leading to conjugated hyperbilirubinemia.
options.explanation: Hepatocytes continuously produce and conjugate bile; obstruction prevents delivery to the duodenum but not hepatic synthesis, so direct bilirubin rises and backs up into blood.

options.label: B
options.text: The gallbladder compensates by synthesizing additional bile salts
options.misconception: The storage organ is being credited with hepatic synthetic capacity.
options.explanation: The gallbladder stores and concentrates bile made by the liver; it cannot synthesize bile salts de novo.

options.label: C
options.text: Pancreatic acinar cells secrete bile when the common bile duct is blocked
options.misconception: An alternate digestive gland is being assigned a hepatic function.
options.explanation: The pancreas secretes enzymatic juice, not bile; continued bile production in cholestasis reflects ongoing hepatic synthesis.

options.label: D
options.text: Duodenal CCK stimulation stops all hepatic bile production until ducts reopen
options.misconception: Hormonal regulation is being cast as a complete shutoff of synthesis.
options.explanation: CCK mainly stimulates gallbladder contraction and pancreatic secretion; hepatic bile production continues despite outflow obstruction.

options.label: E
options.text: Obstruction converts hepatocytes into bile duct epithelium that stores rather than makes bile
options.misconception: A cell-fate change is being proposed instead of continued hepatic synthesis.
options.explanation: Hepatocytes remain the bile source; obstruction impairs excretion, not the synthetic role of the liver.

context: Learning objective: separate bile production from bile delivery. Hepatocytes continuously produce bile; cholestasis blocks excretion, causing conjugated hyperbilirubinemia while synthesis continues.
